notes: Mirrors grammar-replace-0018: the original property is removed, so neither instance can be concluded any more (new_answer null). Functional property: each English personal pronoun (I, you, he, she, it, we, they and their case and reflexive forms) is in exactly one grammatical person. Generic 'you' stays second person and generic 'one' third; singular 'they' is third person (it changes number, not person); inclusive 'we' includes the addressee in meaning but is grammatically first person. The edit is about person only (grammatical number is not functional: 'you' is singular and plural). The near query asks whether the pronoun-person relation is symmetric (no), so its answer differs from the new answer (Rule 7). The derived queries ask whether a second value can also hold (brief: functionality instances ask whether one value excludes another): no before, yes after. Instance facts are stated in the prompt. Avoided base_form_of / singular_of: 'dream' has 'dreamed' and 'dreamt', 'cactus' has 'cacti' and 'cactuses'. All original answers are no, balanced by 0017's yes.
